newsitem.title: CUBA: British official upbeat on Cuba business ties.
newsitem.headline: British official upbeat on Cuba business ties.

text.p: Trade between Britain and Cuba was on the increase and British companies were showing a solid interest in the island, a senior member of Britain's ruling Conservative Party said on Tuesday.

Baroness Young, head of a government and private sector initiative to boost business ties with Cuba, told reporters during a visit that bilateral trade had increased sharply during the first six months of this year.
British exports to Cuba were $29 million, up 92 percent compared with the same period last year, while imports from the Caribbean island were $23 million, up 159 percent, she said.

British firms have invested in oil exploration, tobacco production, soap and detergent production, but exact investment figures are not available. Britain's overseas development finance body, the Commonwealth Development Corporation, is working on a proposal for financing in Cuba.

Young, who met President Fidel Castro for about two hours on Monday evening, led a business delegation including representatives from firms in sectors such as finance and real estate. She said some of the delegation were discussing possibilities for financing restoration work in Havana's historic quarter.

Young said that following her talks with Cuban officials, including central bank president Francisco Soberon, she felt Cuba's economic indicators "demonstrate a positive tendency." "There is much to be done, but British investors are encouraged," she added.

Cuban authorities say the island is heading for Gross Domestic Product growth of around 5 percent this year, after growth of 2.7 percent last year. The economy, sent into a nose-dive by the collapse of Cuba's old economic ally, the former Soviet Union, contracted by more than 35 percent from 1989 to 1993.
